questions.explanation: CIAM advocates separation (correct). New Urbanism advocates MIXING (opposite). CIAM (1933) advocated zoning into four separate functional zones—the doctrine that caused urban dysfunction. New Urbanism (1980s+) is an explicit reaction AGAINST CIAM's separation, advocating mixed-use neighborhoods where residential, retail, services, and offices coexist. They represent opposite values. Transit was not central to CIAM's Athens Charter doctrine (it was written pre-modern transit). New Urbanism incorporates transit integration. New Urbanism emerged as a critique and rejection of CIAM's legacy, not a refinement of it. CIAM (1933) advocated zoning into four separate functional zones—the doctrine that caused urban dysfunction.
